entries.text: A ruler should avoid upsetting the order established by his predecessors.
A ruler should trim policies to circumstances when there is trouble.
A ruler should assume he is of average ability and keep his kingdom for life.
A ruler should not take up arms and rebel against the established order.
A ruler should not damage the interests of those whose support he needs to maintain power.
A well-established ruling family is easier to hold onto than a new one.
A ruler should avoid upsetting the order established by his predecessors.
A ruler should trim policies to circumstances when there is trouble.
A ruler should assume he is of average ability and keep his kingdom for life.
A ruler should eliminate the family of the previous ruler to guarantee his hold on power.
Establishing colonies can be an effective way to hold onto new territory.
Living among the people in the new territory can improve security and stability.
Pampering or destroying people in the new territory can be effective strategies.
Establishing friendly relations with weaker neighbors is crucial.
Undermining stronger neighbors is essential for dominance.
Seeing trouble in advance is key to resolving issues quickly.
A ruler must establish friendly relations with weaker neighboring powers to prevent them from supporting a foreign power.
A ruler must undermine stronger neighboring powers to prevent them from dominating the region.
A ruler must not allow foreign powers to gain influence in the region.
A ruler must not reward good behavior with new territory, as it can lead to weakness.
A ruler must be proactive in anticipating and preventing future problems.
A ruler must not fail to respond to trouble just to avoid war, as this will only put it off to their enemy's advantage.
It is better to take a strong stance and risk war than to appease an enemy and risk losing power.
A ruler should not enhance the power of a stronger state, as this will only make them a greater threat.
A ruler should not bring in a powerful foreign king, as this will only increase their own vulnerability.
A ruler should establish colonies in the territory they have acquired to secure their power.
A ruler should not make promises to other rulers that they cannot keep, as this will only lead to further conflict.
A ruler should not prioritize avoiding war over taking action to secure their power and protect their interests.
A ruler should never fail to respond to trouble just to avoid war.
To help another ruler grow powerful is to prepare your own ruin.
A king is more powerful in a state governed by himself and his ministers than in a state governed by a king and a number of barons.
Unity of command is essential for effective governance.
The type of state being invaded determines the ease of conquest.
Destroying a city is the only sure way to hold it.
Occupation can never extinguish the memory of old institutions.
Measures to win the hearts and minds of the people are futile.
A ruler's ability to stay in power is proportional to their abilities or failings.
A ruler who relies too much on lucky circumstances is less likely to last.
A ruler who imposes a new administrative system and procedures will face initial difficulties.
A ruler who introduces change without solid experience will face opposition.
A ruler who relies on their own resources is more likely to succeed than one who depends on others.

A ruler must establish a strong foundation for their power before attempting to expand it.
A ruler must be cautious of relying on the loyalty of others, as it can be fleeting.
A ruler must be willing to take calculated risks to achieve their goals.
A ruler must be aware of the potential consequences of their actions and plan accordingly.
A ruler must be willing to adapt to changing circumstances and adjust their strategy accordingly.

A ruler's power and influence are key to achieving their goals.
A ruler should be ruthless and talented to achieve their objectives.
A ruler should be able to win over people or destroy them to achieve their goals.
A ruler should build solid foundations for their power to ensure long-term success.
A ruler should be able to respond to aggression with their own forces and talent.
A ruler should not rely on anyone else's armies or authority to achieve their goals.
Effective leadership requires a combination of mental and physical qualities.
Power can be achieved through various means, including violence and manipulation.
Morality is not a necessary component of success, but rather a choice.
Loyalty and mercy are not essential for achieving power, but rather a personal choice.
Talent is not solely defined by one's ability to commit crimes and live without loyalty, mercy, or creed.
A ruler should use cruelty well, being short-lived and decisive, to secure their position and then stop.
A ruler should not use cruelty badly, growing increasingly cruel later on, rather than easing off.
A ruler should assess how much violence and cruelty will be necessary and get it over with at once.
A ruler should win their subjects over with generosity and benefits, rather than violence and cruelty.
A ruler's power is determined by the support of the people or the nobles.
A monarchy can be brought about by either the common people or the nobles.
A king who comes to power with the support of the people has an easier time maintaining power than one who gets there with the support of the nobles.
A ruler must prioritize winning the affection of the common people to maintain power.
A ruler who takes the people under his protection will find it easy to win their loyalty.
A ruler who becomes king against the will of the majority and with the support of the wealthy nobles must make it a priority to win over the affection of the common people.

A ruler's strength is determined by their ability to defend themselves with their own resources.
A well-defended town and a ruler whose subjects don't hate him are less likely to be attacked.
A leader with power and personality can get around problems and rally their subjects.
It's human nature to tie oneself to a leader for the services they've done, rather than the good they've done.
A ruler who is sensible can keep people solid throughout a siege, so long as they have food and weapons.
The Church's temporal power is limited by the short lifespan of popes.
The Church's power is enhanced by the ambition of cardinals.
Mercenary forces are unreliable and should not be relied upon for military defense.
A ruler's power must be based on solid foundations, including good laws and good armed forces.
A ruler must go in person and act as commander himself to ensure effective defense.
A republic must send its citizens to fight, and if a commander is not good, they must replace him.
A ruler or republic with their own armies is more likely to make progress and less likely to fall victim to a coup.
A citizen army is less likely to fall victim to a coup than a republic paying for mercenary armies.
